newsitem.title: ITALY: Patricians of chic in Milan after forays abroad.
newsitem.headline: Patricians of chic in Milan after forays abroad.

text.p: Aristocrats of Italian chic Giorgio Armani and Gianni Versace, fresh from lucrative campaigns abroad, are set to parade their latest womenswear designs on their home turf next week.

Design prince Gianfranco Ferre, trendsetting Miuccia Prada and fashion house Gucci will line up alongside them for Milan's 1997 spring/summer ready-to-wear collections in an eight-day whirlwind of linen and lace.

The shows, which start on Sunday, hot up on Tuesday with leading light Prada unwrapping her latest creations, followed by the Versace second line Istante, then fashion duo Dolce & Gabbana and Krizia on Wednesday.

Gucci, leading the field in luxury style under the guidance of designer Tom Ford, offers its line-up on Thursday. Ferre and Versace will display their main collections on Friday and Saturday and Armani rounds off with his chief designs on Sunday.

But branching out from their classic mainstream collections is becoming a growing activity among some Italian designers, with top names like Versace set to launch a fragrance and Ferre planning a line of mens' accessories.
Milan's sartorial elite, well entrenched in economically sluggish Europe, is also eyeing lucrative U.S. markets, with a flurry of activity in New York in September and October.
Armani recently opened a new flagship store and a new outlet for his second line Emporio Armani in New York.

Talking this week to Reuters at Emporio in central Milan, he said he wanted to expand the line in the United States, deeming Emporio broadly more appropriate than the higher priced Giorgio Armani label.
"Emporio Armani comes in offering a more suitable level," he said. Europe is not abandoned, however, with France "holding more space to expand" and openings in other countries planned.
The Emporio Armani collection will take to the catwalk at the silver-haired designer's palatial headquarters on Thursday.
Rival Versace opened his flagship outlet in New York in September, as did Valentino, fabric design house Etro and Moschino. Prada too has a new store opening there in October.
The run-up to the 1997 season shows has been marked also by a mild spat between Armani and Versace, following a comment to a magazine by Armani, 62, that fashion was finished.
Versace, 50, snapped back that periodically there were fashion designers who suddenly discovered fashion was dead, "perhaps confusing overall appreciation with a personal problem."
Armani has since said he was quoted out of context and meant a fashion system of style dictated from above was over. "Modern fashion is about freedom, democracy and individualism," he said.
The shows will have their usual mix of sylphlike supermodels and celebrity spectators.
Italian media said while many stylists were likely to ditch the fashion world's latest gimmick of putting celebrities on the catwalk, the odd famous name might pop up.
One such is 15-year old Ivanka Trump, daughter of U.S. billionaire Donald and his first wife Ivana, who is set to sashay for Enrico Coveri.
